clause_i.reason: For the map-brush mode across generated seeds, the same action history does not identify the seed-dependent displaced boundary parcel or canton pair, so an action-only q(I_t) cannot generally select the visible repair. This is static screenshot dependence only and supplies no changing task state.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded window of 0 ms containing the current screenshot is sufficient in principle: the map visibly contains parcel geometry, current canton colors, guild marks, and joined borders, while the ledger exposes the population, holding, budget, and brush rules. No prior frame is needed; this is an ordinary static visual planner.

clause_iii.reason: No autonomous outcome-relevant task-state evolution occurs during an idle delay. Parcel assignment changes only in pointer event handlers, and the 100 ms CSS fill transition is action-triggered presentation after the assignment is committed. The shared clock or 240-second play allowance alone cannot create the required strict loss in Q or action advantage, so no Delta > 0 and legitimate D can satisfy this clause.

common_visible_process: None. The only visible change after an outcome-affecting action is a short CSS fill interpolation; it does not alter assignment, connectivity, population, holdings, action availability, or action value. The global virtual clock has no charter-specific callback to evolve the task.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the label. This task has no autonomous outcome phase to defer actions into.

source_evidence.claim: The assigned difficulty-1 profile has 9 columns by 6 rows (54 parcels), one balanced singleton exchange, a 6-change budget, and population tolerance 1; its full natural-language control requires a 2-parcel joined stroke with at least 1 repaint.
Full interaction is implemented as a canton-seal selection plus direct adjacent-parcel brushing, and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The runtime exposes one-frame observations, a 0 ms observation window, a 240-second play allowance, and mouse/keyboard action channels.
Generation constructs the warped target, initial displaced assignment, polygons, and guild assignments once from a seeded random generator; there is no episode-time update loop.
The generator returns a static public state containing parcels, adjacency, initial assignment, guilds, and parameters, while target assignment remains in ground truth.
The browser renders a fixed SVG parcel map, visible parcel colors/guild marks, boundaries, and nine canton seal buttons from the loaded state.
Assignment and brush changes are performed synchronously by recordAssignment/brushParcel during event handling; brush paths are restricted to adjacent parcels and then committed on pointerup.

Full mode binds only pointer drag events and seal clicks for gameplay, while undo synchronously restores history and certification submits the current transcript; no mechanic timer or animation-frame callback is scheduled.
The only timed visual effect for parcels is a 0.1 s fill/fill-opacity CSS transition, with no task-state movement or changing hit geometry.
The shared controller virtualizes timers and requestAnimationFrame and drains only callbacks registered by page code; its generic polling/animation loop does not itself mutate a mechanic.
The grader replays the visible event transcript, assignment changes, undo history, geometry, budget, connectivity, population, and guild split; it has no task-time or timestamp-based outcome rule.
The verifier only loads the exported result and invokes the independent replay grader, then reports its pass/fail result.
The used shared helper loads the mechanic grader and grades the exported result; it contributes no autonomous task behavior.

The implementation solver reads the static initial/target assignments, computes a finite repair list, performs the required brush, and certifies; its private target access is implementation evidence rather than policy information.
